record.title: RSI-Prime reports decision-level supervision gains for autonomous model-training agents
record.summary: A 17 November preprint introduces RSI-Prime, a dataset reported to contain 350 complete model-training trajectories across seven task categories, and decision-level quality annotations for selecting training supervision. On PostTrainBench v1.2, the authors report that full-trajectory SFT raises a GLM-5.3 training agent’s weighted score from 36.56 to 45.61, while decision-level SFT reaches 48.24 and retains 75.48% of supervised tokens. The result is from one harness/model/resource regime, includes disclosed HumanEval content overlap, and has not been independently reproduced here; it does not establish open-ended recursive self-improvement.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors submitted arXiv:2611.23138v1 on 17 November 2026, describing a dataset and training method for improving agents’ model-training capability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports RSI-Prime as 350 complete experimental trajectories spanning seven task categories, with decision-level identification and quality annotation used to mask supervision on low-quality behavior while retaining full experimental context.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On PostTrainBench v1.2, the authors report that full-trajectory fine-tuning raises the GLM-5.3 training agent’s weighted score from 36.56 to 45.61, while decision-level SFT reaches 48.24 (31.95% relative gain over the original agent). Decision SFT retains 75.48% of supervised tokens and scores 2.63 points above full SFT.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a human audit of 400 randomly sampled decision records, reviewed independently by two annotators with third-reviewer adjudication; post-adjudication acceptance was 98.75% for decision identification, 99.50% for action classification, and 97.50% for quality assessment. The sample does not estimate omitted-decision recall.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected preprint does not establish independent replication, transfer across training agents or harnesses, or sustained recursive self-improvement beyond the reported PostTrainBench setup.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched replication of full SFT versus decision-level SFT on RSI-Prime was inspected.
The paper reports one training-agent/harness regime and does not establish transfer to other training agents, harnesses, or sustained iterative improvement.
The paper notes training/evaluation content overlap for HumanEval, one of six weighted tasks in the PostTrainBench aggregate.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported result holds in its bounded regime, decision-level supervision from complete model-training trajectories could improve agents that conduct post-training experiments and influence how research agents are trained. The paper does not demonstrate recursive or open-ended self-improvement.
limitations: The reported performance results are author claims from one preprint and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The experiment uses a GLM-5.3 agent in the DeepSeek Harness with one NVIDIA H100 and a cumulative 10-hour execution budget; transfer across models, harnesses, or longer horizons is not established.
The authors disclose training–evaluation content overlap for HumanEval, one of six benchmark tasks.
The 400-record human audit samples already identified records and does not estimate recall of omitted decisions.
The original GLM-5.3 reference row averages three runs per benchmark; the paper’s summary does not establish equivalent independent repetitions for every fine-tuned comparison.
brief.summary: A 17 November preprint introduces RSI-Prime, a dataset reported to contain 350 complete model-training trajectories across seven task categories, and decision-level quality annotations for selecting training supervision. On PostTrainBench v1.2, the authors report that full-trajectory SFT raises a GLM-5.3 training agent’s weighted score from 36.56 to 45.61, while decision-level SFT reaches 48.24 and retains 75.48% of supervised tokens. The result is from one harness/model/resource regime, includes disclosed HumanEval content overlap, and has not been independently reproduced here; it does not establish open-ended recursive self-improvement.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report PostTrainBench v1.2 weighted scores of 36.56 for original GLM-5.3, 45.61 after full-trajectory SFT on RSI-Prime, and 48.24 after decision-level SFT. Decision SFT retains 75.48% of supervised tokens and exceeds full SFT by 2.63 aggregate points; the paper reports gains on each of six task scores. HumanEval-related content appears in the training corpus and overlaps one evaluated task.
technical.compute_or_cost: The evaluated training agent uses DeepSeek Harness, one NVIDIA H100 GPU and a cumulative 10-hour agent-execution budget per experiment; the paper does not establish monetary economics or scaling beyond this regime.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public arXiv v1 preprint specifies the dataset construction, decision annotation/masking method, evaluation setup and reported results. This activation inspected those sections but did not independently reproduce them.
technical.mechanism: RSI-Prime collects complete model-training trajectories, identifies experimental decisions, annotates action type and decision quality, and masks assistant messages linked to decisions that fail the quality-selection rule during selective supervised fine-tuning. The full context remains available while only selected assistant messages contribute to loss.
technical.novelty: Applies fine-grained decision-level quality supervision to full experimental trajectories as a way to improve an agent’s ability to conduct model post-training; the paper compares it with full-trajectory, tool-failure and step-level masking at similar supervision volumes.
technical.regime: The paper fine-tunes GLM-5.3 as a training agent and evaluates target Qwen3-4B-Base models across six PostTrainBench v1.2 tasks using DeepSeek Harness, one NVIDIA H100 and a cumulative 10-hour agent budget. The weighted aggregate uses official task weights. The authors note HumanEval-related training–evaluation content overlap.
technical.strongest_baseline: The original GLM-5.3 agent scores 36.56 on the paper’s weighted aggregate; full-trajectory SFT scores 45.61 and decision-level SFT scores 48.24. The paper reports three valid independent reference runs per task for original GLM-5.3; this does not establish the same repetition count for all tuned agents.

brief.title: RSI-Prime reports decision-level supervision gains for autonomous model-training agents
brief.why_it_matters: The work studies whether agents can learn better model-training decisions from full experimental histories instead of imitating every recorded action or selecting only by step/tool outcome. If its bounded PostTrainBench result replicates, decision-quality supervision could improve research-agent post-training; current evidence does not show autonomous recursive improvement, cross-harness transfer, or real-world research productivity.
